summary: Iteration 3 (Smart Filters + Budget Tracking) tested end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 new pytest cases pass covering (a) GET /api/expenses date_from/date_to inclusive YYYY-MM-DD lexical range, (b) q case-insensitive regex across vendor/remarks/product_line, (c) combining q+main_category+payment_status+date range, (d) POST /api/budgets upsert (second POST for same {month, main_category} updates amount, no duplicate), (e) GET /api/budgets?month filter, (f) DELETE /api/budgets/{id} soft delete removes from GET list, (g) GET /api/dashboard?month includes budget block with has_budgets/total_budget/total_spent/by_category each containing category/budget/spent/remaining/pct, (h) has_budgets=false when month omitted OR month has no budgets, (i) seeded May 2026 budget (Milk Procurement Cost 50000 vs actual 55000 => pct 110.0) verified. Frontend (390x844 mobile viewport): Dashboard auto-opened May 2026 and renders 'Budget vs actual' card showing ₹55,000 of ₹50,000 with red '₹5,000 over budget' label and the Milk Procurement Cost per-category bar. Expenses screen: typing 'verka' in the search input (testID expenses-search) debounces for 300ms then filters list to 2 Verka Dairy rows (₹55,000, excludes Patna Electricity Board); clear-X button resets search; funnel icon (testID expenses-filter-button) opens the bottom-sheet modal (Filters title) with Category picker (expenses-filter-category), From/To DateFields, Clear all + Apply buttons. Manage screen now shows the 3rd segment 'Budgets'; it exposes the budget-month picker, per-category budget inputs (budget-input-marketing, etc.) and the budget-save button. All 7 feature items from the request have been verified.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py upsert_budget: no validation that main_category exists in CATEGORY_HIERARCHY. User could create a budget for a typo category and it would persist and show on dashboard with spent=0. Low priority - built-in UI only exposes known categories.
server.py upsert_budget: no validation that amount >= 0; a negative amount is accepted and would yield negative remaining + nonsensical pct. Consider enforcing >=0 at the Pydantic layer.
server.py dashboard budget block: pct is capped at >100 (e.g. 110%) in the response but the UI progress fill is capped at Math.min(pct, 100) which is correct. Just noted for consistency.

manage.tsx BudgetsTab save(): skips categories whose current input is empty or 0 and skips when the existing value already equals val. This means users cannot zero-out an existing budget by clearing the input - they'd have to delete the budget via DELETE endpoint (no UI for that). Minor UX gap.
manage.tsx BudgetsTab: 'Saved ✓' flag only turns on if save() runs synchronously; it does not wait for mutation success, so the checkmark appears even on failure. Low priority.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 3 new UI flows (dashboard budget-vs-actual card, expenses search+filter sheet, manage Budgets segment)
